purpose: Reconcile the new official Waterloo source statements with the earlier cross-check, and make a conservative materiality disposition for remaining secondary-only candidates. No new original statement is claimed in this pass.

records.title: Cranes

evidence.observation: The October 4, 2008 Waterloo archive page lists Problem A: Cranes.

The full statement specifies a square-grid construction site, candidate crane locations with rotation radii, non-touching crane safety constraints, and maximizing total covered area; at most 15 candidate locations.

records.note: This corrects the earlier pass-16 wording: the statement is a geometric non-overlap selection problem over at most 15 candidate locations. The official contest statement is real; the exact Kattis slug mapping is still not established.

records.title: Exact Change

evidence.observation: The October 4, 2008 Waterloo archive page lists Problem C: Exact Change.
The full statement minimizes payment at or above the purchase price, then the number of bills/coins; price <= 10000 cents, at most 100 items.

records.note: The official Waterloo source statement is verified. It does not independently prove the Kattis `exactchange2` crosswalk. `exactchange3` is a distinct Kattis variant and is not a substitute.

records.title: Walrus Weights

evidence.observation: The Kattis entry identifies source Popup 2015 Session 1 and author Marc Vinyals.
A published solution shows subset-sum reachability and selecting a total nearest 1000; it is implementation evidence, not statement evidence.
A problem discussion describes choosing a subset of plate weights whose sum is closest to 1000; it is not an authoritative statement.

records.note: The available technical evidence points to a single bounded subset-sum target-nearest-1000 task, not a multi-stage scenario. This is only a provisional materiality judgement; the original Popup statement and constraints remain unavailable.

records.title: Word Cloud

evidence.observation: The exact title/slug is mapped to MCPC 2014; the distinct Word Clouds Revisited task is mapped to MCPC 2015.
Full statement mirror inspected, including typography formulas, ordered greedy row packing, input/output, constraints, and examples.
Problem metadata identifies MCPC USA 2014 Regional Contest and authors Ryan Marshall and Michael Goldwasser.

records.note: The candidate's STRONG label is not supported. The narrative includes typography calculations and row layout, but the core is one ordered greedy packing procedure. Original contest-hosted statement and human rubric review remain pending. Do not confuse `wordcloud` with `wordclouds`.
